p-mn43-19.3.en: When a mendicant has entered the first absorption, placing the mind, keeping it connected, rapture, bliss, and unification of mind are present.
p-mn43-19.3.pi: Idhāvuso, paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa bhikkhuno vitakko ca vattati, vicāro ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca.

p-mn43-20.2.en: “The first absorption has given up five factors and possesses five factors.

p-mn43-20.3.en: When a mendicant has entered the first absorption, sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt are given up.
p-mn43-20.3.pi: Idhāvuso, paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti;

p-mn43-20.4.en: Placing the mind, keeping it connected, rapture, bliss, and unification of mind are present.

p-sn11.3-10.2.en: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
p-sn11.3-10.2.pi: “svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.

p-sn46.1-1.12.en: They develop the awakening factor of equanimity, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.
p-sn46.1-1.12.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.1-1.4.en: In the same way, a mendicant develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors depending on and grounded on ethics, acquiring great and abundant good qualities.
p-sn46.1-1.4.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṁ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto mahantattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti dhammesu.

p-sn46.1-1.6.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.
p-sn46.1-1.6.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ;

p-sn46.11-1.3.en: In the same way, a mendicant develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors depending on and grounded on ethics.
p-sn46.11-1.3.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṁ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti.

p-sn46.11-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.11-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.12-1.2.en: In the same way, for a mendicant good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the arising of the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.12-1.2.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ uppādāya etaṁ pubbaṅgamaṁ etaṁ nimittaṁ, yadidaṁ—kalyāṇamittatā.

p-sn46.12-1.3.en: A mendicant with good friends can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.12-1.3.pi: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

p-sn46.12-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.12-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.13-1.2.en: In the same way, for a mendicant rational application of mind is the forerunner and harbinger of the arising of the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.13-1.2.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ uppādāya etaṁ pubbaṅgamaṁ etaṁ pubbanimittaṁ, yadidaṁ—yonisomanasikāro.

p-sn46.13-1.3.en: A mendicant accomplished in rational application of mind can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.13-1.3.pi: Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

p-sn46.13-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.13-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.130-1.10.en: “… which have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination …”

p-sn46.130-1.11.en: “… which slant, slope, and incline to extinguishment …

p-sn46.130-1.12.en: The seven awakening factors should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.”
p-sn46.130-1.12.pi: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ uddhambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ime satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvetabbā”ti.

p-sn46.130-1.4.en: Desire for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, desire for rebirth in the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance.

p-sn46.130-1.6.en: The seven awakening factors should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.
p-sn46.130-1.6.pi: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ uddhambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvetabbā.

p-sn46.130-1.9.en: and equanimity, which culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion. …”

p-sn46.17-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.
p-sn46.17-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṁ gamanāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.17-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.17-1.4.en: These seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.
p-sn46.17-1.4.pi: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṁ gamanāya saṁvattantīti.

p-sn46.19-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they are noble and emancipating, and bring one who practices them to the complete ending of suffering.
p-sn46.19-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā nīyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya.

p-sn46.19-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.19-1.4.en: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they are noble and emancipating, and bring one who practices them to the complete ending of suffering.”

p-sn46.20-1.1.en: “Mendicants, the seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.
p-sn46.20-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.20-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.20-1.4.en: These seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”
p-sn46.20-1.4.pi: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.21-2.3.en: “Mendicant, they’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.
p-sn46.21-2.3.pi: “‘Bodhāya saṁvattantī’ti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā bojjhaṅgāti vuccanti.

p-sn46.21-2.4.en: A mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

p-sn46.21-2.5.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.21-2.5.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.21-2.6.en: They’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.”

p-sn46.22-1.1.en: “Mendicants, I will teach you the seven awakening factors.

p-sn46.22-1.3.en: And what are the seven awakening factors?

p-sn46.22-1.4.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.24-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind irrationally, sensual desire,
p-sn46.24-1.1.pi: “Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati;

p-sn46.24-1.2.pi: anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati;

p-sn46.24-1.3.pi: anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati;

p-sn46.24-1.4.pi: anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati;

p-sn46.24-1.5.en: and doubt arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.
p-sn46.24-1.5.pi: anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati;

p-sn46.24-1.6.en: And the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity don’t arise, or if they’ve already arisen, they cease.
p-sn46.24-1.6.pi: anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati …pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati.

p-sn46.24-2.1.en: When you apply the mind rationally, sensual desire,
p-sn46.24-2.1.pi: Yoniso ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando nuppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando pahīyati;

p-sn46.24-2.5.en: and doubt don’t arise, or if they’ve already arisen they’re given up.
p-sn46.24-2.5.pi: anuppannā ceva vicikicchā nuppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā pahīyati.

p-sn46.24-3.1.en: And the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity arise, and once they’ve arisen, they’re fully developed.”
p-sn46.24-3.1.pi: Anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati …pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī”ti.

p-sn46.25-1.7.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.26-1.1.en: “Mendicants, you should develop the path and the practice that leads to the ending of craving.
p-sn46.26-1.1.pi: “Yo, bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā taṇhakkhayāya saṁvattati, taṁ maggaṁ taṁ paṭipadaṁ bhāvetha.

p-sn46.26-1.4.en: It is the seven awakening factors.

p-sn46.26-1.6.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.”

p-sn46.26-2.1.en: “Udāyī, it’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.
p-sn46.26-2.1.pi: “Idha, udāyi, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ vipulaṁ mahaggataṁ appamāṇaṁ abyāpajjaṁ.

p-sn46.26-2.5.en: A mendicant develops the awakening factor of equanimity, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.
p-sn46.26-2.5.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ vipulaṁ mahaggataṁ appamāṇaṁ abyāpajjaṁ.

p-sn46.27-1.1.en: “Mendicants, you should develop the path and the practice that leads to the cessation of craving.
p-sn46.27-1.1.pi: “Yo, bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā taṇhānirodhāya saṁvattati, taṁ maggaṁ taṁ paṭipadaṁ bhāvetha.

p-sn46.27-1.4.en: It is the seven awakening factors.

p-sn46.27-1.6.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.27-2.2.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.27-2.2.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.27-2.3.en: This is how the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated so as to lead to the cessation of craving.”
p-sn46.27-2.3.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṁ bahulīkatā taṇhānirodhāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.28-1.1.en: “Mendicants, I will teach you a path that helps penetration.

p-sn46.28-1.5.en: It is the seven awakening factors.

p-sn46.28-1.7.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.”

p-sn46.28-1.9.en: “Sir, how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to lead to penetration?”
p-sn46.28-1.9.pi: “kathaṁ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṁ bahulīkatā nibbedhāya saṁvattantī”ti?

p-sn46.28-2.1.en: “Udāyī, it’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.
p-sn46.28-2.1.pi: “Idha, udāyi, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ vipulaṁ mahaggataṁ appamāṇaṁ abyāpajjaṁ.

p-sn46.28-2.5.en: A mendicant develops the awakening factor of equanimity, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.
p-sn46.28-2.5.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ vipulaṁ mahaggataṁ appamāṇaṁ abyāpajjaṁ.

p-sn46.28-2.9.en: This is how are the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated so as to lead to penetration.”
p-sn46.28-2.9.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, udāyi, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṁ bahulīkatā nibbedhāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.29-1.1.en: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that, when it is developed and cultivated like this, leads to giving up the things that tighten the fetters like the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.29-1.1.pi: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi, yo evaṁ bhāvito bahulīkato saṁyojanīyānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya saṁvattati, yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā.

p-sn46.29-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.29-2.2.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.29-2.2.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.29-2.3.en: That’s how the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated so as to lead to giving up the things that tighten the fetters.
p-sn46.29-2.3.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṁ bahulīkatā saṁyojanīyānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.31-1.1.en: “Mendicants, whatever qualities are skillful, part of the skillful, on the side of the skillful, all of them are rooted in diligence and meet at diligence, and diligence is said to be the best of them.
p-sn46.31-1.1.pi: “Ye keci, bhikkhave, dhammā kusalā kusalabhāgiyā kusalapakkhikā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṁ dhammānaṁ aggamakkhāyati.

p-sn46.31-1.2.en: A mendicant who is diligent can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.31-1.2.pi: Appamattassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

p-sn46.31-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.31-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.32-1.1.en: “Mendicants, whatever qualities are skillful, part of the skillful, on the side of the skillful, all of them are rooted in rational application of mind and meet at rational application of mind, and rational application of mind is said to be the best of them.
p-sn46.32-1.1.pi: “Ye keci, bhikkhave, dhammā kusalā kusalabhāgiyā kusalapakkhikā, sabbe te yonisomanasikāramūlakā yonisomanasikārasamosaraṇā; yonisomanasikāro tesaṁ dhammānaṁ aggamakkhāyati.

p-sn46.32-1.2.en: A mendicant accomplished in rational application of mind can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.32-1.2.pi: Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

p-sn46.32-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.32-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.33-2.1.en: In the same way, there are these five corruptions of the mind. When the mind is corrupted by these it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant. It’s brittle, and not rightly immersed in samādhi for the ending of defilements.
p-sn46.33-2.1.pi: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime cittassa upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṁ cittaṁ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṁ, na ca pabhassaraṁ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṁ khayāya.

p-sn46.33-2.3.en: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
p-sn46.33-2.3.pi: Kāmacchando, bhikkhave, cittassa upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhaṁ cittaṁ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṁ, na ca pabhassaraṁ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṁ khayāya …pe…

p-sn46.33-2.4.en: These are the five corruptions of the mind. When the mind is corrupted by these it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant. It’s brittle, and not rightly immersed in samādhi for the ending of defilements.”
p-sn46.33-2.4.pi: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca cittassa upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṁ cittaṁ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṁ, na ca pabhassaraṁ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.

p-sn46.34-1.1.en: “Mendicants, these seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.
p-sn46.34-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.34-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.34-1.3.pi: Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.34-1.4.en: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”
p-sn46.34-1.4.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.35-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind irrationally, sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”
p-sn46.35-1.1.pi: “Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati; anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati; anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati; anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati; anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.

p-sn46.35-2.1.en: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind rationally, the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity arise, and once they’ve arisen, they’re fully developed.”
p-sn46.35-2.1.pi: “Yoniso ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati …pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī”ti.

p-sn46.36-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to growth and progress.
p-sn46.36-1.1.pi: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā buddhiyā aparihānāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.36-1.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.36-1.4.en: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to growth and progress.”
p-sn46.36-1.4.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā buddhiyā aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.

p-sn46.37-1.1.en: “Mendicants, there are these five obstacles and hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.
p-sn46.37-1.1.pi: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā.

p-sn46.37-1.3.pi: Kāmacchando, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo cetaso upakkileso paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo.

p-sn46.37-1.4.pi: Byāpādo, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo cetaso upakkileso paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo.

p-sn46.37-1.5.pi: Thinamiddhaṁ, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ cetaso upakkilesaṁ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṁ.

p-sn46.37-1.6.pi: Uddhaccakukkuccaṁ, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ cetaso upakkilesaṁ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṁ.

p-sn46.37-1.7.pi: Vicikicchā, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā.

p-sn46.37-1.8.en: These are the five obstacles and hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.
p-sn46.37-1.8.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā.

p-sn46.37-2.1.en: There are these seven awakening factors that are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.
p-sn46.37-2.1.pi: Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti.

p-sn46.37-2.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.37-2.3.pi: Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.37-2.4.en: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”
p-sn46.37-2.4.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattantīti.

p-sn46.38-1.1.en: “Mendicants, sometimes a noble disciple pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to the teaching. At such a time the five hindrances are absent, and the seven awakening factors are fully developed.
p-sn46.38-1.1.pi: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti, imassa pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṁ samaye na honti. Satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṁ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.

p-sn46.38-2.1.en: What are the five hindrances that are absent?
p-sn46.38-2.1.pi: Katame pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṁ samaye na honti?

p-sn46.38-2.2.en: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
p-sn46.38-2.2.pi: Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṁ tasmiṁ samaye na hoti, byāpādanīvaraṇaṁ tasmiṁ samaye na hoti, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṁ tasmiṁ samaye na hoti, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṁ tasmiṁ samaye na hoti, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṁ tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.

p-sn46.38-3.1.en: And what are the seven awakening factors that are fully developed?
p-sn46.38-3.1.pi: Katame satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṁ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti?

p-sn46.38-3.2.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.38-3.2.pi: Satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

p-sn46.38-3.4.en: Sometimes a noble disciple pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to the teaching. At such a time the five hindrances are absent, and the seven awakening factors are fully developed.”
p-sn46.38-3.4.pi: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti, imassa pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṁ samaye na honti. Ime satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṁ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchantī”ti.

p-sn46.40-1.1.en: “Mendicants, these five hindrances are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.
p-sn46.40-1.1.pi: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhiyā anibbānasaṁvattanikā.

p-sn46.40-1.3.en: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
p-sn46.40-1.3.pi: Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṁ, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇaṁ acakkhukaraṇaṁ aññāṇakaraṇaṁ paññānirodhikaṁ vighātapakkhiyaṁ anibbānasaṁvattanikaṁ.

p-sn46.40-1.8.en: These five hindrances are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.
p-sn46.40-1.8.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhiyā anibbānasaṁvattanikā.

p-sn46.40-2.1.en: These seven awakening factors are creators of vision and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.
p-sn46.40-2.1.pi: Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññābuddhiyā avighātapakkhiyā nibbānasaṁvattanikā.

p-sn46.40-2.3.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.40-2.3.pi: Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññābuddhiyo avighātapakkhiyo nibbānasaṁvattaniko …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññābuddhiyo avighātapakkhiyo nibbānasaṁvattaniko.

p-sn46.40-2.4.en: These seven awakening factors are creators of vision and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.”
p-sn46.40-2.4.pi: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññābuddhiyā avighātapakkhiyā nibbānasaṁvattanikā”ti.

p-sn46.41-1.2.en: “Mendicants, all the ascetics and brahmins in the past who have given up the three discriminations have done so by developing and cultivating the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.41-1.2.pi: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahiṁsu, sabbe te sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

p-sn46.41-1.3.en: All the ascetics and brahmins in the future who will give up the three discriminations will do so by developing and cultivating the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.41-1.3.pi: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahissanti, sabbe te sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

p-sn46.41-1.4.en: All the ascetics and brahmins in the present who are giving up the three discriminations do so by developing and cultivating the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.41-1.4.pi: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahanti, sabbe te sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

p-sn46.41-1.6.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.41-1.9.en: and present who give up the three discriminations do so by developing and cultivating the seven awakening factors.”
p-sn46.41-1.9.pi: pajahanti, sabbe te imesaṁyeva sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā”ti.

p-sn46.43-1.1.en: “Mendicants, I will teach you a path for crushing Māra’s army.

p-sn46.43-1.5.en: It is the seven awakening factors.

p-sn46.43-1.7.en: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

p-sn46.43-1.8.en: This is the path for crushing Māra’s army.”

p-sn46.48-1.2.en: In the same way, for a mendicant good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the arising of the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.48-1.2.pi: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ uppādāya etaṁ pubbaṅgamaṁ etaṁ pubbanimittaṁ, yadidaṁ—kalyāṇamittatā.

p-sn46.48-1.3.en: A mendicant with good friends can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.48-1.3.pi: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

p-sn46.48-1.6.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.48-1.6.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.49-1.1.en: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that gives rise to the seven awakening factors like rational application of mind. …”
p-sn46.49-1.1.pi: “Ajjhattikaṁ, bhikkhave, aṅganti karitvā nāññaṁ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ uppādāya, yathayidaṁ—bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro.

p-sn46.5-1.11.en: They’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.”

p-sn46.5-1.5.en: “Mendicant, they’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.

p-sn46.5-1.6.en: A mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.5-1.6.pi: Idha, bhikkhu, satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.5-1.7.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.5-1.7.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.50-1.1.en: “Taking into account exterior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that gives rise to the seven awakening factors like good friendship. …”
p-sn46.50-1.1.pi: “Bāhiraṁ, bhikkhave, aṅganti karitvā nāññaṁ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ uppādāya, yathayidaṁ—bhikkhave, kalyāṇamittatā.

p-sn46.51-1.2.en: “Mendicants, I will teach you what fuels and what starves the five hindrances and the seven awakening factors.
p-sn46.51-1.2.pi: “Pañcannañca, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇānaṁ sattannañca bojjhaṅgānaṁ āhārañca anāhārañca desessāmi;

p-sn46.51-1.5.en: There is the feature of beauty.

p-sn46.51-1.6.en: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

p-sn46.51-10.2.en: There is tranquility of the body and of the mind.

p-sn46.51-10.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to that

p-sn46.51-11.2.en: There are things that are the basis of serenity and freedom from distraction.

p-sn46.51-11.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to them

p-sn46.51-12.2.en: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of equanimity.

p-sn46.51-12.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to them

p-sn46.51-13.2.en: There is the feature of ugliness.

p-sn46.51-13.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to that

p-sn46.51-14.2.en: There is the heart’s release by love.

p-sn46.51-14.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to that

p-sn46.51-15.2.en: There are the elements of initiative, persistence, and exertion.

p-sn46.51-15.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to them

p-sn46.51-16.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to that

p-sn46.51-17.2.en: There are qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.
p-sn46.51-17.2.pi: Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā sāvajjānavajjā dhammā hīnapaṇītā dhammā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā.

p-sn46.51-17.3.en: Frequent rational application of mind to them

p-sn46.51-18.2.en: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of mindfulness.

p-sn46.53-10.1.en: When the mind is restless, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.
p-sn46.53-10.1.pi: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-10.3.en: Because it’s hard to settle a restless mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-10.3.pi: Uddhataṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi duvūpasamayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.53-13.1.en: When the mind is restless, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.53-13.1.pi: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-13.3.en: Because it’s easy to settle a restless mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-13.3.pi: Uddhataṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi suvūpasamayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.53-15.4.en: But mindfulness is always useful, I say.”

p-sn46.53-4.1.en: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.
p-sn46.53-4.1.pi: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-4.3.en: Because it’s hard to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-4.3.pi: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.53-7.1.en: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.
p-sn46.53-7.1.pi: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.

p-sn46.53-7.3.en: Because it’s easy to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.
p-sn46.53-7.3.pi: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.

p-sn46.57-1.2.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.57-1.2.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā.

p-sn46.57-1.4.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of a skeleton together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.57-1.4.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…

p-sn46.57-1.5.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.57-1.5.pi: aṭṭhikasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.57-1.6.en: That’s how the perception of a skeleton, when developed and cultivated, is very fruitful and beneficial.”
p-sn46.57-1.6.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhikasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā”ti.

p-sn46.57-2.1.en: “When the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
p-sn46.57-2.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññāya, bhikkhave, bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.

p-sn46.57-3.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great benefit.
p-sn46.57-3.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-4.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great sanctuary from the yoke.
p-sn46.57-4.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-5.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great inspiration.
p-sn46.57-5.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.57-6.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to dwelling in great ease.
p-sn46.57-6.1.pi: “Aṭṭhikasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.7-1.2.en: In the same way, a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.
p-sn46.7-1.2.pi: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.

p-sn46.7-2.3.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.7-2.3.pi: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.7-2.4.en: That’s how a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”
p-sn46.7-2.4.pi: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti.

p-sn46.70-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of dissatisfaction with the whole world is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.71-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.72-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of suffering in impermanence is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.73-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of not-self in suffering is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.74-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of giving up is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.75-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of dispassion is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

p-sn46.76-1.1.en: “Mendicants, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.76-1.1.pi: “Nirodhasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā.

p-sn46.76-1.3.en: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,
p-sn46.76-1.3.pi: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …pe…

p-sn46.76-1.4.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-1.4.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-1.5.en: That’s how, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated, it’s very fruitful and beneficial.
p-sn46.76-1.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsāti.

p-sn46.76-2.1.en: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results:
p-sn46.76-2.1.pi: Nirodhasaññāya, bhikkhave, bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—

p-sn46.76-2.2.en: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
p-sn46.76-2.2.pi: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.

p-sn46.76-2.6.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-2.6.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-2.7.en: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated in this way you can expect one of two results:
p-sn46.76-2.7.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitāya kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññāya evaṁ bahulīkatāya dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—

p-sn46.76-2.8.en: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
p-sn46.76-2.8.pi: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitāti.

p-sn46.76-3.1.en: “The perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.
p-sn46.76-3.1.pi: Nirodhasaññā, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati, mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati, mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati, mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattati.

p-sn46.76-3.4.en: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
p-sn46.76-3.4.pi: nirodhasaññāsahagataṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

p-sn46.76-3.5.en: That’s how the perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.”
p-sn46.76-3.5.pi: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, nirodhasaññā evaṁ bahulīkatā mahato atthāya saṁvattati, mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati, mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati, mahato phāsuvihārāya saṁvattatī”ti.
